videos.title: Doosan SMX 3100 9 AXIS TOOLING, SETUP & MACHINING DEMO
videos.description: Multi-episode live event showing full machining of a Ti-6Al-4V titanium part on the SMX 3100 9-axis mill-turn. Covers tooling, programming with Mastercam mill-turn module, chuck transfer, coolant strategy, 5-axis milling operations, CMM inspection with Mitutoyo.

videos.title: Incredible 5 Axis Tool Paths on 9 Axis Doosan Mill/Turn Episode 2
videos.description: Episode 2 continuation. Detailed walkthrough of 5-axis toolpath programming in Mastercam mill-turn module, blade expert paths, pinch turning, stock models, code expert syncing, machine simulation. Inspection segment with Mitutoyo Crysta Apex 5-axis CMM.

videos.title: Haas Control Training Video
videos.description: Complete NGC (Next Generation Control) training: startup procedure, hand jog, feed/speed overrides, program management, offset setup, VPS probing for work offsets, VPS G-code generation, settings, diagnostics, help system, tool management.

videos.title: Haas Make This Part On Day One
videos.description: Complete first-part workflow on Haas TL (Tool Room Lathe). Tool offset setup (X diameter measure, Z face measure), VPS/Shape Creator programming, collision avoidance, single block proving, G54/G55 work offsets for multi-op parts.

videos.title: Haas ST-20Y Setup Video
videos.description: Full dual-spindle setup on Haas ST-20Y with Y-axis. Tool eye probing system for automatic tool offset setting, G10 stored offsets for repeat jobs, sub-spindle tool setup, bolt-on tool center line, Z face measure on sub-spindle with finished part reference.

videos.title: Secrets to Running a SMX3100 9 Axis Mill Turn
videos.description: Mastercam programming techniques for the SMX 3100/2100. 3D OptiRough with spindle-coordinated motion, avoidance geometry, transform & rotate for multi-face operations, quick C-plane, morph toolpath for chamfers with 5-axis output, collision control with holder/shank checking.

videos.title: Titanium Part on 9 AXIS MILL/TURN Speeds & Feeds PUMA SMX3100
videos.description: Titanium speeds and feeds on the SMX3100. No auto-generated subtitles available for this video.

upper_milling_head.description: Like a 3-axis mill with B-axis tilt. X up/down, Y in/out across the part, Z along the spindle axis, B-axis back and forth for angle cuts on either side.

lower_turret.description: Like a standard 2-axis lathe with live tooling capability. Same as PUMA lathe configuration with bolt-on live tools and regular turning tools.

sub_spindle.description: A-axis moves sub-spindle in and out to grab longer/shorter parts, enables part transfer between spindles.

c_axes.c1: Main spindle rotation (becomes 5th axis when combined with upper head B-axis)
c_axes.c2: Sub-spindle rotation (independent 5th axis for sub-spindle operations)

effective_configurations.main_spindle_5axis: Upper head (X,Y,Z,B) + C1 = full 5-axis milling on main spindle
effective_configurations.sub_spindle_5axis: Upper head (X,Y,Z,B) + C2 = full 5-axis milling on sub-spindle
effective_configurations.turning: Lower turret (X,Z) for standard turning on either spindle
effective_configurations.pinch_turning: Lower turret + upper head turning simultaneously from both sides

milling_spindle.description: True milling spindle, not like live tooling (typically 5-7K RPM, 10HP). Can aggressively machine titanium, Monel, Inconel.

tool_magazine.advantage: No need for expensive live tool holders. Any angle, any tool — just program and tool change.

main_spindle.chuck_type: Schunk THW Plus (quick jaw change chuck)
main_spindle.mechanism: Quarter-turn allen wrench release, safety mechanism prevents wrench removal without jaw
jaw_types_used: Impact series claw jaws (vampire jaws) for raw stock
Soft bored jaws for finish operations

sub_spindle.reason_6_jaw: Thin-wall parts need contact around entire surface; 3 jaws leave unsupported areas that deflect

work_envelope.notes: Steady rest available for long parts. Range from 8-inch chucks to 5-meter bed lengths across SMX family.

programming.dual_program_structure: Two separate programs run simultaneously — one for upper head, one for lower turret
programming.sync_mechanism: Code Expert in Mastercam: link operations between upper/lower streams, define when each stream starts/waits
programming.plane_management: Mill-turn auto-creates work planes from selected geometry; no manual plane setup for most operations
programming.stock_models: Generate after each operation to see remaining material; use as input for subsequent toolpaths to avoid air cutting

process_planning.sequence_pattern: Alternate between lathe ops (lower turret) and mill ops (upper head)
typical_flow: 1. Face and rough turn OD (lower turret, CNMG insert)
2. Face mill / high-feed mill flats or hex (upper head, 2-inch face mill)
4. Rough mill features — slots, pockets (upper head, Harvey One TE end mill)
5. Finish mill — ball tracking (upper head, Harvey Three ball end mill)
6. Drill operations (upper head, Kennametal WiTech drill)

g54_management.note: Separate G54 offsets for lower turret AND upper turret. When moving part (e.g., facing to adjust position), BOTH G54s must be updated by same amount.
g54_management.chuck_transfer: Additional G54 set to front of sub-spindle jaws; must also be updated if main-spindle part position changes.

pinch_turning.description: Simultaneous turning from both lower turret and upper head, pinching the part from both sides
pinch_turning.use_case_1: Long skinny parts: equalizes cutting forces from both sides, prevents deflection, allows heavier cuts
pinch_turning.use_case_2: Cycle time reduction: removes material at twice the rate since both tools are cutting simultaneously
pinch_turning.programming: Mastercam mill-turn: 'Pinch Turn Main' + 'Pinch Turn Associated' toolpaths linked together

blade_expert.description: Specialized Mastercam path for airfoil/impeller shapes with repeating blades around a hub
blade_expert.inputs: Hub floor surface, blade splitter surfaces, fillets, number of segments
blade_expert.cutting_style: Full slotting, aggressive roughing in 2 depth cuts
blade_expert.automation: Automatically patterns around part based on segment count

multi_axis_pocketing.description: Dynamic style motion with constant cutter engagement for rest roughing
multi_axis_pocketing.advantage: More efficient tool engagement vs blade expert
multi_axis_pocketing.trade_off: More programming time but better tool motion and tool life

3d_optirough_with_spindle.description: 3D OptiRough where spindle (C-axis) rotates coordinated with tool motion
3d_optirough_with_spindle.setup: Select C-axis face + upper left spindle in setup tab
3d_optirough_with_spindle.example: Tool cuts on OD while spindle rotates — effectively uses all 9 axes for roughing

morph_toolpath.description: Multi-axis morph between two curves for chamfer or radius finishing
setup_steps: Select two boundary curves (e.g., top and bottom of chamfer)
Set zigzag cutting method for continuous motion
Collision control: flute trim + holder avoidance

transform_and_rotate.description: Program one face, then rotate/mirror to other faces automatically
transform_and_rotate.critical_note: Ensure lead-outs and clearances give enough space to fully retract before rotation
transform_and_rotate.saves: Program once, apply to all symmetric faces

simulation.importance: Critical for 9-axis — too many moving components to visualize mentally
requirements: Fully modeled machine including sheet metal enclosure
All tool holders modeled (KM50 holders from Kennametal on lower turret)
Accurate tool lengths and shank dimensions
Chuck jaw geometry for clearance checking
clearance_checks: Lower turret to chuck jaws at max Z-minus position
B-axis head tilt clearance to chuck jaws
Tool shank to hex walls during 5-axis motion

general_sfm_range.peripheral_milling: 400-500 SFM possible with trochoidal/peripheral milling (Harvey Three end mills)

turning_roughing.stock_allowance: 5 thou on face, 5 thou on OD for finish
turning_roughing.notes: G96 constant surface speed, RPM increases as diameter decreases. Conservative for live camera.

face_milling_high_feed.notes: High-feed geometry allows shallow aggressive cuts. Light harmonic rumble at this feed — increasing feed would eliminate it.

slot_roughing_5axis.tool: Harvey One TE end mill, 3/8 inch, 60 thou corner radius
slot_roughing_5axis.strategy: 5-axis roughing with C-axis rotation coordinated with tool motion

slot_finishing_5axis.tool: Harvey Three ball end mill, 3/8 inch (Duo Lock 6-flute)
slot_finishing_5axis.strategy: Ball tracking — starts at top of slot, works down
slot_finishing_5axis.motion: Full 5-axis simultaneous, C-axis turning along with part as tool traces slot angle

id_bore.size: 1.25 inch (also mentions 1.5 inch on different feature)

advantages: Clear — allows visual monitoring of cut (important for education/filming and real machining)
Essential for titanium — without coolant, titanium will catch fire during milling
Used across all machines in Titans facility
coolant.delivery: Through-spindle high pressure for drilling and deep feature operations

chip_control.target: Short, broken chips — not long stringy ones
chip_control.method: Dial in feed rate so chips break cleanly. Too low feed = long stringy chips wrapping around tool/part.
chip_control.safety_note: NEVER reach into machine to remove stringy chips with bare hands — they cut like razor wire

end_mills: Harvey Three — ball end mill finishing
tooling_used.pricing_reference: Harvey end mills starting at $41 (3/8 inch) and $56 (1/2 inch) at time of video

startup_procedure: 1. Cycle the door (open/close) to verify door switch
4. Press Power Up (blue button) to home all axes
5. Press Cancel to clear startup checklist screen

key_buttons.feed_hold: Pause program (does NOT lose position or reset program)
key_buttons.reset: Clear alarms, reset program to start
key_buttons.recover: Recovery from tool change failure or mid-change E-stop — answers yes/no questions to recover

hand_jog.axis_selection: X, Y, Z, plus B, C on equipped machines
hand_jog.jog_lock: Press jog lock to feed continuously at selected rate without holding button

override_controls.handle_feed: 1% increments using hand wheel when engaged
override_controls.haas_recommendation: 25% rapid override when proving new programs

mode_selections.edit: Edit G-code, functions: insert/alter/delete/undo, F1 menu (save, copy, paste, search, find/replace, line numbers)
mode_selections.memory: Run program mode. Options: single block, graphics (2D simulation), option stop (M01), block delete (/ prefix)
mode_selections.mdi: Manual Data Input — type and execute short code sequences, probing
mode_selections.zero_return: Home axes. Options: All (like power up), Single (individual axis), G28
mode_selections.list_program: Select/manage programs. Navigate: Memory, USB, Network tabs

program_management.loading_from_usb: List Program > USB tab > Select file > Enter > F2 (OK) > Go to Memory tab > Enter to load to memory
program_management.warning: Loading from USB makes USB the active source — program tries to run FROM USB. Always switch to Memory tab before running.
program_management.erase: Select program > checkmark > Erase Program > confirm
program_management.copy_from_usb: List Program > USB > find file > F2 copy > select Memory destination > Enter

display_screens.program: Active codes, tool info, coolant level, override %, position, timer/counter

position.all_tab: Shows all 4 position displays simultaneously — recommended when proving new programs

offset.tool_offsets: Length, diameter, wear. Note: in-spindle indicator shows active tool. Scroll right for flute count (for chip load display), probing data.
offset.work_offsets: G54-G59 etc. Access via F4 shortcut or arrow navigation. Shows X, Y, Z plus B, C on equipped machines.

current_commands.atm: Automatic Tool Management — redundant tooling setup
current_commands.calculator: Standard, milling speed/feed calculator, tapping calculator

alarms.alarm_viewer: Look up any alarm number description, F1 search
alarms.key_history: Time-stamped keystroke log — verify what was actually typed

diagnostics.system: Serial number, software revision, power-on time
diagnostics.maintenance: Loop cycles, force lubrication (F2/F3), coolant refill

settings.navigation: Cursor through settings, search function (type keyword > F1)
settings.network: Wired/wireless setup, net share, HaasConnect app, remote display
settings.user_positions: Second-home, tool change position, table positions
settings.user_travel_limits: Jog to limit position > F2 to store as soft limit

help.features: Table of contents, G-code lists, programming examples
help.sample_programs: Can copy from help and paste into program

vps_probing.description: Visual Programming System — guided probing and G-code generation

work_offset_probing.navigation: Edit > top > VPS > Probing > Work Offsets

steps: Enter X/Y incremental distance from corner (e.g., 0.5 inch)
Enter Z travel distance for probe descent
Hand jog probe over corner (eyeball position)
Cycle Start — probes top face, then X/Y work offsets

gcode_generation.navigation: Edit > top > VPS > right arrow > select operation type

output_options: F4: Insert to clipboard (paste into existing program)
Create new program (asks for O-number, name, comment)

important_settings_referenced.setting_53: Jog Without Zero Return — allows jogging before machine is homed (useful for clearing turret)
important_settings_referenced.ssb: Single Spindle Brake (referenced as example search term)

lathe_axis_conventions.critical_note: ALL X values are in DIAMETER, not radius. Point at 0.5 inch from center = X1.0

drill_x_offset.method: Indicate center of drill holder front-to-back, highlight offset, press X Diameter Measure, enter 0

turning_x_offset.method: Skim OD of stock, jog away in Z+, measure diameter with mic/caliper, highlight offset, press X Diameter Measure, enter measured diameter

turning_z_offset.method: Skim Z face, jog away in X, highlight offset, press Z Face Measure

drill_z_offset.method: Jog drill to face of part using shim/paper drag test, highlight offset, press Z Face Measure. Optionally subtract shim thickness.

work_offset_setup.op10: G54 — X=0, Z=0 set where tools were touched off (spindle center line and part face)
work_offset_setup.op20: G55 — second operation after flipping part

vps_shape_creator.purpose: Define part profile graphically for lathe operations
workflow: Edit > Shape Creator > Origin for new shape
Enter XZ coordinates for each profile point as new rows
Select motion type: linear feed, rapid, arc
Import into VPS OD Roughing template

key_parameters.raw_dimensions: Define green box (raw stock). Example: X3.0, Z0.05
key_parameters.rapid_point: Where tool rapids to before feeding. Set just outside stock (e.g., X3.1, Z0.1). Critical: rapid point and profile start must share same Z value.
key_parameters.contour_start: First profile point. X must account for tool nose radius (TNR). For 0.031 TNR: X = -0.062 (diameter value).
key_parameters.tool_nose_compensation: If programmed to X0 instead of X-0.062, leaves nib/pip on face. Must go below center by TNR amount (in diameter).

parameters.work_offset: G54 for op1, G55 for op2
parameters.max_rpm: Set to 1000 for first parts (safety limit)
parameters.surface_speed: From insert manufacturer data (entered 1601 SFM — limited by max RPM)
parameters.stock_removal_cycle: 71 for OD roughing, 0 for finish pass
parameters.feed_rate: 0.016 IPR (may bump to 0.020 to break stringy chips)
parameters.retract_home: NO — especially on TL with long tools. Set safe tool change position instead (e.g., X3.1, Z8.0)
parameters.end_m_code: M1 (optional stop between operations), M30 for last operation

collision_avoidance_checklist: 1. During tool change: turret must be far from chuck, tailstock, and doors
2. At home position: verify long tools clear all obstructions
3. Turning at max Z-minus: check that other turret tools don't hit chuck jaws
4. Jog to furthest Z-minus programmed position and visually verify clearance
5. Use 5% rapid override + single block for first run
6. Stop about 1 inch from part, check Distance To Go display
7. If Distance To Go says -5 inches but you're only 1 inch away — STOP. Something is wrong.
proving_procedure: 1. Run graphics simulation first — look for rapids through part or weird moves
2. Verify T-numbers match turret positions (T101 = turning, T202 = spot drill, T303 = long drill)
5. Cycle start through each line, watching tool approach
6. Feed hold when ~1 inch from part
7. Check Position > Distance To Go — verify reasonable
8. Continue single block through first few roughing passes
9. Turn off single block when cycle looks safe
10. Enable option stop (M01 after each operation) — check coolant, chips, part

haas_st20y_setup.machine: Haas ST-20Y (dual spindle with Y-axis live tooling)

key_features.part_transfer: Full part transfer from main to sub-spindle in single operation

tool_eye_probing_system.description: Automatic tool offset setting using built-in tool eye probe
tool_eye_probing_system.activation: Edit > Probing system > Set Tool Offsets > Turning Tools > Manual (for first setup)
tool_eye_probing_system.tool_eye_deploy_retract: F2 toggles between extended/retracted. ALWAYS retract before indexing turret.
process_per_tool: 1. MDI > index to desired turret position (T101, T303, etc.)
2. Edit > F2 twice to deploy tool eye
3. Set tool number and offset number
4. Set tool tip direction (3=OD facing, 2=ID boring, 7=drill centerline, 4=sub-spindle OD)
5. Controller shows diagram of correct approach direction
6. Hand jog tool to ~0.250 inch (6mm) from probe per instruction
7. Cycle Start — tool eye measures (double-touch: initial + accuracy pass)
9. Edit > F2 to retract tool eye
10. Power Up + A (return to safe position)
tool_eye_probing_system.bolt_on_drill_x_center: After Z probe, go to Offsets > highlight X geometry > press F3 (Set to Bolt-on Center Line). Machine knows center line for bolt-on tools.

g10_stored_offsets.description: Pre-stored work offsets in program. Dramatically reduces setup time for repeat jobs.
g10_stored_offsets.benefit: With same jaws (stamped 1/2/3, loaded in same position) + G10 offsets, setup becomes: touch off tools + load material + go.
g10_stored_offsets.example: G10 lines at program start set G54, G55, G56 etc. for main and sub-spindle operations.
g10_stored_offsets.combined_savings: Jaw change: minutes instead of re-boring. Offsets: already close. Tool eye: fast automatic touch-off.

back_side_turning_tool.offset_convention: Same turret position (T1) but different offset number (T1/21 instead of T1/01)
back_side_turning_tool.process: Same as front but tip direction 4 for sub-spindle OD cutting

back_side_boring_bar.problem: Cannot physically touch boring bar to tool eye (wrong direction)
back_side_boring_bar.x_solution: If boring bars on positions 6 and 24 use same holder size, copy X geometry offset from front boring bar to back boring bar (same X dimension)
back_side_boring_bar.z_solution_option_1: Run part, stop before back boring bar runs, touch off to part face, Z Face Measure
back_side_boring_bar.z_solution_option_2: Use finished reference part: MDI > G56 B-3.0 (move sub-spindle to machining position) > hand jog boring bar to finished part face using paper drag > Z Face Measure with part reference length

sub_spindle_z_touch_off.method: Move sub-spindle to machining position via G-code (e.g., G56 B-3.0), then touch tool to known reference part face
sub_spindle_z_touch_off.critical_concept: Z0 is face of part, so sub-spindle must be in machining position (not home) when touching off
sub_spindle_z_touch_off.measurement_example: Tool at Z = -6.938 from home to part face

tooling_used.grooving: Iscar TangGrip (extra reach for deeper grooves)
tooling_used.boring: Kennametal 3/4 boring bar, CCMT insert, 1 thou TNR

jaw_management.stamping: Stamp jaws 1, 2, 3 and always load in same position on same machine
jaw_management.runout: Fresh material will show wobble (not machine surface yet) — this is normal
jaw_management.benefit: Saving stamped jaws + G10 offsets = dramatic setup time reduction on repeat jobs

tips.description: Use 3D OptiRough toolpath with C-axis face selection and upper left spindle to make spindle rotate with tool. Tool cuts on OD while spindle coordinates — effectively wrapping roughing motion around the part.
setup_steps: Select machining geometry (e.g., 3 faces using Ctrl+click for similar surfaces)
Set containment to OD of part
In Setup tab: select 'C-axis face' + 'upper left spindle'
Use stock model from lathe operations
Steep/shallow: force max and min depth to same value (e.g., 2.4 inch) for single-depth pass
Set avoidance geometry AFTER first generation to see what tool tries to do, then restrict
tips.avoidance_geometry_tip: Generate toolpath first without avoidance, see where rapid lines go wrong, then set avoidance to exclude those areas. Approach varies by part geometry.

tips.description: Program a 2D or any pass on one face, then use Transform Rotate to copy it to other faces at specified angles. Spindle rotates automatically in posted code.
tips.critical_warning: Ensure lead-outs and clearances retract tool fully before rotation. If tool isn't clear when spindle rotates, collision will occur.
tips.time_savings: Only program one instance of feature, transform handles the rest

tips.description: Right-click part surface in Mastercam > Quick C Plane > selects surface and creates tool plane with Z pointing outward. Instant plane setup for any angled face.
tips.best_practice: RENAME quick C-planes after creation. Otherwise you get many 'Quick C Plane 1' and 'Quick C Plane 2' entries that are impossible to identify later.

details.tool_stick_out: Must stick out farther than usual for multi-axis — tool rotates significantly and needs clearance to chuck/part
details.cut_pattern: Morph between two curves (outside and inside edges of chamfer)
details.cutting_method: Zigzag (stays on part, alternating direction each pass)
details.extended_trim: Start 50% of tool diameter off the chamfer edge

collision_control.flute: Trim and re-link on collision with machining geometry
collision_control.holder_shank_shoulder: Retract along tool axis if close to avoidance geometry (outside of part)

details.linking: Default links follow surfaces; adjust lead-in/lead-out as needed

tips.machine_model_in_sim: Full SMX 3100 with chucks, turrets, magazine
what_to_verify: Tool tilting and spindle coordinated motion
No purple in toolpath (indicates linking/gap issues)
Tool clearance to chuck jaws during B-axis rotation
Full path verification before going to machine

shop_floor_cmm.design: Open design for large/long parts, future robot loading

lab_cmm.model: Mitutoyo Crysta Apex with PH-20 5-axis head
lab_cmm.angular_resolution: Less than 1 degree increments (vs old 7.5/15/22.5 degree lock points)
lab_cmm.head_touch: Moves probe head without moving entire machine — faster measurement, faster calibration
lab_cmm.accuracy: 2.2 microns, under 3 microns with extended stylus
lab_cmm.probe_rack: 6-station with standard force, medium force, EM-1, EM-2, light force, 6-way modules

inspection_workflow.operator_interface: Quick Launcher touch screen — select part by picture
inspection_workflow.alignment: CNC alignment: 4-point plane on top, circle on OD for origin, edge for clocking

scanning.contour_scan: ~288-290 points around profile from CAD model path
scanning.measurement_perpendicular: Measures perpendicular to tangent at each CAD model point

inspection_workflow.threaded_hole_measurement: Chase threads out incrementally to stay in major diameter — without chasing, measurement shifts to minor diameter

complex_feature_measurement.flutes_slots: Section at 3 different heights to detect deflection or path deviation
complex_feature_measurement.rationale: Part may flex more at free end — 3 sections reveal if cutting path deviated at different depths

reporting.pass: Green OK in corner, optional no-print when all good
reporting.fail: Print only bad features (not full 300-feature report)

cell_configuration.door: Servo door (robot enters as door opens, exits as door closes — saves cycle time vs pneumatic)
cell_configuration.workholding: Schunk pneumatic vise (air to open/close via M-code)

robodrill_specs.tool_changer: 21 tools, 0.7 second tool change, 1.2 second chip-to-chip
robodrill_specs.tapping: Up to 8,000 RPM rigid tapping, 1.6 seconds back-out

gripper_design.custom_fingers: Designed in-house, 3D printed for testing, then machined from aluminum on DNM 5700L
gripper_design.dual_diameter: 2.0 inch OD raw stock + 1.9 inch finished step — robot goes deeper for finished part pickup
gripper_design.profile: Low profile with ball-track surface for trunnion clearance

vise_jaws.design: Low profile ball-track surface for 5-axis clearance

process_flow: 1. Robot picks puck from table (future: conveyor)
3. Robot enters, places in pneumatic vise
4. 0.5 second wait timer before vise closes (prevents premature grip)
6. Machine runs program (engraving + chamfer with air blast)
7. Air blast cleans chips from part and vise
8. Door opens, robot enters, vise opens (with wait timer)
9. Robot removes part, places on output table

mill_turn_advantages: Complete part in one setup — no moving between machines
Eliminates fixture design for milling (chuck IS the fixture)
Reduces scrap from re-fixturing and re-alignment
One operator can run the machine while it produces complete parts
Automation-ready with bar feeder and parts catcher
Flexible: landing gears, bolt carrier assemblies, valves, tubes with features
Not just for aerospace — any job shop moving parts between lathe and mill benefits
tool_change_safety_on_lathes: Never command tool change near chuck, tailstock, or doors
Verify long tools won't hit anything at home position
Set safe tool change position far in front of part (e.g., Z+8 inches)
Check that non-active turret tools clear chuck jaws at maximum Z-minus cutting position
mastercam_mill_turn_key_concepts: Separate program streams for upper head and lower turret
Sync operations in Code Expert — link start of one stream to completion of another
Plane management largely automatic — derived from selected geometry
Stock models between operations for visualizing and optimizing subsequent toolpaths
Transform/Rotate for symmetric features around C-axis
Full machine simulation with modeled holders is essential for clearance verification

haas_essential_lathe_codes.referenced_as: Essential Nine Lines document (linked in Haas video descriptions)
haas_essential_lathe_codes.g96: Constant surface speed (CSS) — RPM varies with diameter
haas_essential_lathe_codes.m01: Optional stop (pause between operations for checking)

key_formulas_and_values.tool_nose_radius_compensation: X value must go below centerline by TNR amount (in diameter). 0.031 TNR = program X-0.062
key_formulas_and_values.high_feed_milling_titanium: 200 SFM, 0.012 per tooth chip load, 0.025 inch DOC
